key_insight: Attention-sink positions in diffusion language models shift substantially across denoising steps, so pruning heuristics that preserve static AR-style sinks are suboptimal; a sink-aware importance metric that accounts for trajectory variance enables much more effective pruning.
problem_solved: Reduces the high inference cost of Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) by providing a principled pruning method tailored to DLMs — addressing the mismatch between autoregressive pruning heuristics and diffusion-specific attention dynamics.
method: Empirically measure attention-sink behavior across the full denoising trajectory and quantify per-position/attention variance.
Define a sink-aware importance score that aggregates step-wise dominance and variance to rank tokens/heads/units for retention.
Prune models using the sink-aware scores (static or step-aware masks), then fine-tune or calibrate to recover generation quality while reducing FLOPs/latency.
impact: Gives practitioners a principled, diffusion-specific pruning strategy that lowers DLM inference cost and latency without sacrificing generation quality, enabling more practical deployment of diffusion-based LLMs.
visual_elements: Timeline heatmap of attention across denoising steps showing shifting sink locations vs. a static AR sink baseline.
Bar chart of model FLOPs/latency vs. generation quality (perplexity/accuracy) comparing AR-based pruning and sink-aware pruning.
Schematic showing sink-aware scoring → pruning mask → lighter model pipeline.
Attention-head/position variance plot highlighting which components are stable vs. trajectory-dependent (to justify pruning choices).
paper_title: Sink-Aware Pruning for Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Aidar Myrzakhan, Tianyi Li, Bowei Guo, Shengkun Tang, Zhiqiang Shen
